Print/export Download as PDF Printable version In other projects Wikimedia Commons Wikidata item Appearance move to sidebar hide From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia 12th-century Lord of Montpellier William VIII of Montpellier Died 1202 ( 1203 ) Noble family Guilhem Spouses Eudokia Komnene Agnes of Castile Father William VII of Montpellier Mother Matilda of Burgundy William VIII (in Occitan : Guilhem; died 1202) was Lord of Montpellier , the son of William VII and Matilda of Burgundy . William VIII married Eudokia Komnene , grand-niece of the Byzantine emperor Manuel I Komnenos . [ 1 ] They had one daughter, Marie of Montpellier . Lacking a male heir, William separated from Eudokia, sending her to a monastery in Ariane. Adalaïs. The Pope ruled William's marriage to Agnes as illegitimate and Marie was given the throne. [ 5 ] William VIII was a patron of troubadours . Arnaut de Mareuil came to his court after fleeing from the entourage of Azalais of Toulouse , and at least one of Arnaut's poems is addressed to him.
